subject: acorn woodpecker
title: This Woodpecker Family Drills 50,000 Holes in One Tree, Then Fills Them

scenes.text: A woodpecker family drilled fifty thousand holes in one tree.
Acorn woodpeckers hammer one acorn into each hole. It's their winter food.
A tree like that can take up to a hundred years. Each generation inherits it and keeps drilling.
Then the acorns dry and shrink. So the birds pull the loose ones and move them to smaller holes.
They'll use anything wooden. One landowner found 485 pounds of acorns in his water tank.
In an empty house, they packed the door and window frames with 62,264.

description:
A single family of acorn woodpeckers can drill up to 50,000 holes in one tree and fill each with an acorn.
These granary trees are built and maintained over many generations, and a 50,000-hole granary may have taken as long as a century. As stored acorns dry and shrink, the birds move the loose ones to smaller holes, and the whole group defends the store. They also use utility poles, fence posts and wooden buildings: 485 pounds of acorns were once recovered from a wooden water tank, and 62,264 acorns were counted in the door and window casings of an unused house.
Where is the strangest place you have seen an animal hide food? Comment below.
first_comment: In shared nests, each female destroys the eggs already there before she lays her own, so over a third of the eggs are lost. Where is the strangest place you have seen an animal hide food?
